Prevention: Proper land preparation (deep ploughing) control pupal stage.
Removal of host plants and weed management can also control the population of
Sowing of attractant plants on crop border side, so birds are attracted to feed on larvae i.e. millet (bajra), sunflower.
Crop rotation should be done for at least 2-3 years.
Timely sowing of crop and proper spacing should maintained.
Monitoring: Monitor crop during the budding, flowering, pod formation and maturity.
Inspect twice weekly from early budding until late podding.
Sample six widely-spaced locations per field.
Pheromone traps should be used to monitor moths.
These traps attract male moths using the sex pheromone (methyl eugenol).
Light traps are used to check the population of
Convert larval counts/m to larvae/m2 by dividing counts by the row spacing in metres.
Small larvae should be scouted for by inspecting (opening) vegetative terminals and flowers.
Helicoverpa defoliation is characterised by rounded chew marks and holes.
Direct Control: Trichogramma 7-8 cards/acre can be used in field.
The larvae are controlled well when less than 7 mm (rice grain size).

Netelia (wasps) i.e. caterpillar parasites, species of tachinid flies i.e. caterpillar parasites.
Spine predatory bug, glossy shield bug, damsel bug, big eyed bug, apple dimpling bug, assassin bug, red and blue beetle.
Restrictions: The safe handling of pesticides must be followed.
Always wear protective clothing, and do not eat or smoke when spraying dangerous chemicals.
